- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or slowly rising, expect overshoot or overconfidence; correct by adding 1–2% downward bias in early horizon.
- If true outcomes show sharp upward spikes after low prices (e.g., 68→75+), model often underreacts — adjust forecast to include 3–5% lagged momentum or add 1–2% upward bias in next 5–7 days.
- When supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model tends to underpredict price rise — apply 1–3% upward bias to early forecast if sentiment is weak.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts are rising, expect mean reversion — reduce forecast slope by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from 15-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 15-day trend (not 30-day) to avoid horizon mismatch.
- When multiple auction events occur in 7–14 days, model often overestimates supply impact — reduce forecast by 1–3% per event if supply net is negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to overfit recent sentiment — use 3-day moving average of sentiment to smooth and avoid overreaction.
